qs.q: Which of the following interventions is part of the specific cause-directed management for Wilson disease in a patient with cirrhosis?
qs.e: Penicillamine is used specifically for the management of Wilson disease in established cirrhosis. Phlebotomy is instead indicated for hemochromatosis.

qs.q: A patient with suspected Wilson's disease presents with liver disease and neuropsychiatric symptoms. Which combination of laboratory tests assists in confirming this genetic disorder?
qs.e: Wilson's disease involves copper accumulation and is diagnosed using caeruloplasmin and 24-hr urinary copper tests. Ferritin and transferrin saturation are instead used to diagnose haemochromatosis.
qs.s: Clinical Chemical Pathology Crash Course — Part 2: MCQs

qs.q: A patient presenting with features of chronic hepatitis is investigated for metabolic hereditary causes. Which of the following pairs of investigations targets Wilson's disease?
o: Anti-nuclear antibodies and serum globulin levels
Serum ceruloplasmin and 24-hour urine for copper
Serum alpha-1 antitrypsin level and phenotype
Transferrin saturation and HFE gene analysis
qs.e: Wilson's disease is investigated using serum ceruloplasmin and 24-hour urine for copper. Transferrin saturation and HFE gene testing are used for hemochromatosis.

qs.q: A patient is investigated for hereditary metabolic causes of chronic hepatitis. Which laboratory tests are specific for diagnosing Wilson's disease?
o: Transferrin saturation and serum ferritin levels
qs.e: Wilson's disease is investigated using serum ceruloplasmin and copper measurements, as well as a 24-hour urine collection for copper. Hemochromatosis is evaluated via transferrin saturation, ferritin, and HFE genes.

qs.q: Wilson's disease is caused by ATP7B mutations leading to
qs.e: Autosomal recessive. Copper accumulates in liver (cirrhosis), basal ganglia, eyes (Kayser-Fleischer rings), kidneys. Serum ceruloplasmin LOW. Treatment: D-penicillamine or trientine.

qs.q: Kayser-Fleischer rings in Wilson's disease represent
qs.e: Golden-brown rings at corneal periphery. Best seen on slit-lamp. Pathognomonic of Wilson's with neurologic involvement. Present in >95% with neurologic disease.
